Subject: Post-renewal verification: dedicated pool scale test window

Hi Jane / Orion ops team,

Thanks again for finalizing the renewal this week — excited to have the additional committed capacity in place. Per the amended contract we reserved a dedicated GPU pool for Orion (reservation ID: ORH-POOL-2026-47). Before we close the loop on the amendment, we need to run the post-renewal validation so you can sign off on the throughput guarantees.

Proposed test window: Thu 2026-02-17 16:00 - 18:00 PT (2 hours) — please confirm.
What we'll run: a tiered load profile that ramps to sustained 1,200 concurrent inference sessions (90k tokens/min aggregated), with bursts up to 2,000 sessions for brief intervals to validate autoscale headroom.
Acceptance criteria (summary):
- 95th pct latency <= 220ms token-gen under sustained load
- 99th pct latency <= 600ms with no tail degradation longer than 60s
- No more than 2% error rate (5xx/timeout)
- Throughput matches reserved pool baseline (8 additional A100 equivalents added)

I've attached the load-test plan (load-test-plan-20260210.pdf) and the amendment that contains the updated reserved-capacity terms. Lauren from Renewals is cc'd to help with any billing/procurement items.

If the window above works, we'll coordinate with your on-call for any escalation and with Karthik from infra to provision the extra GPUs into the dedicated pool before test start.

Thanks — Sean

Subject: Load test results & initial analysis

Team / Orion ops,

We executed the planned run on 2026-02-17 16:00-17:50 PT. Summary below — raw CSV and latency traces attached (p95-latency-traces-20260217.zip).

Results (high level):
- Sustained load: 1,200 concurrent sessions achieved for 60 minutes; aggregate token rate ~92k tokens/min.
- p95 token-gen latency: 198ms (meets <= 220ms target).
- p99 token-gen latency: 540ms with two short spikes hitting ~720ms for 18s during a synthetic burst from one region.
- Error rate: 0.9% transient 5xx observed during the two spikes; otherwise <0.2%
- Throughput: measured baseline matches the expected reserved capacity; autoscale headroom validated up to burst of 2,050 sessions for 30s without preempting other tenants.

Notes on the p99 spikes: traced to a KV cache cold-start from a rare model path when the burst drove new context shapes. We primed KV caches and re-ran a 10-minute synthetic exercise; no recurrence observed. Action items: add a short warm-up stage to the standard run (we'll include that in the plan going forward).

Operational handoff:
- Dashboard: https://redwood.monitoring/orion/ORH-47/dashboard (contains p95/p99 and token throughput timeseries)
- On-call contact (Redwood infra): infra-oncall@redwood.com (pager: +1 888 555-0006)
- Suggested alert thresholds: p95 > 240ms, p99 > 700ms, error-rate > 2%

Conclusion: The expanded dedicated pool meets the acceptance criteria aside from brief p99 tail spikes that are mitigated by the warm-up step. Recommend acceptance signature.

--
Karthik Iyer
